source.title: Continual Learning Through Synaptic Intelligence
source.venue: Proceedings of the 34th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 70:3987-3995

confidence_rationale: Demonstrates that a purely parameter-level, online-accumulated importance signal (each synapse integrates its own contribution to loss reduction over training) suffices to consolidate prior tasks and substantially prevent catastrophic forgetting, matching EWC, without any per-event admission gate or held write-eligible state. This supports the Q-062 side that a consolidation-priority mechanism (REE MECH-285 / MECH-094) -- not an explicit MECH-368 write-eligible state -- can carry the load of preventing undifferentiated global updates. Down-weighted because it is a conference model on MNIST-scale task sequences, and 'substantially prevents' is not 'prevents on REE's online world-model path'.
failure_signatures: Synaptic intelligence prevents forgetting via a regularisation prior on weight changes, not via gating which weights are eligible to change at a given event; it shows consolidation-priority can work WITHOUT an explicit write-eligible state, but does not test whether such a state would add value on top.

The importance measure is accumulated continuously and re-read as a penalty -- consistent with Q-062 sub-question (2)'s 'salience tag re-read' option rather than a held intermediate state with its own entry/exit; offered as the cheaper hypothesis, not a refutation of MECH-368.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Assigning each synapse an online-computed importance (the path integral of its gradient-times-update contribution to loss) and penalising changes to important weights enables a network to learn sequential tasks while preserving earlier ones, matching Elastic Weight Consolidation on permuted/split MNIST and far exceeding plain SGD.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports Q-062's hypothesis that consolidation-priority by accumulated importance (REE: MECH-285 consolidation-priority by V_s residual; MECH-094 provenance) is a sufficient mechanism to avoid catastrophic interference WITHOUT an explicit event-level write-eligible state (MECH-368). Maps onto the 'existing combination already suffices' branch of the falsifier.
mapping.mapping_caveat: An importance-weighted regulariser is a parameter-level prior re-read at update time, not REE's online admission gate on a non-stationary world-model/policy stream; 'substantially prevents forgetting on MNIST-scale task sequences' does not establish sufficiency on REE's online path, and the paper does not directly contrast a held write-eligible state against its absence.
mapping.source_context: Feedforward networks, permuted MNIST (10 tasks) and split MNIST (5 tasks); online per-synapse importance accumulation.

confidence_components.notes: Source_quality solid (foundational, heavily cited ICML method, but a conference paper on MNIST-scale benchmarks). Mapping_fidelity moderate: it is the consolidation-priority analogue but does not test the held-state-vs-no-state contrast that is the heart of Q-062. Transfer_risk substantial: small-benchmark parameter regulariser -> REE online world-model write path.
